no_target_yet.statement:
Assume (H1) and admissibility. The distributions insensitive at level
$c_0$ are exactly $\ker D\cap\simplex$. Their affine dimension is
$m-\operatorname{rank}D-1$, and $\pi$ is the unique such distribution
if and only if $\operatorname{rank}D=m-1$.

no_target_yet.next_step: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.reason: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.statement:
Let $2\leq N<m$, with $A,\pi,\beta$ as above. For every admissible
$D\in\mathcal D$, there are interior insensitive distributions
$q\ne\pi$ arbitrarily close to $\pi$. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\operatorname{rank}D\leq m-2$, a nonconstant line segment
through $\pi$ consists of interior distributions at level $c_0$.
\item If $\operatorname{rank}D=m-1$, necessarily $N=m-1$, and there is
a continuous curve of interior distributions $q(\lambda)$ for all
sufficiently small real $\lambda$, with
\[
 q(0)=\pi,\qquad Dq(\lambda)=\lambda Aq(\lambda),\qquad
 C(q(\lambda),\gamma)=\frac1{1+\beta+\lambda}.
\]
For $\lambda\ne0$, $q(\lambda)\ne\pi$. This conclusion does not require (H1).
\end{enumerate}

no_target_yet.statement:
Fix $N=m\ge2$, a strictly positive invertible $A$, an interior prescribed
distribution $\pi$ and $\beta>0$. Assume (H1), that all $f_\nu$ are
nonnegative, and that at each $\gamma$ some $f_\nu(\gamma)>0$.
For each $k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ there is a nonempty relatively open subset of
$\mathcal D$ on which $B>0$, $A^{-1}D$ has distinct real eigenvalues, and
there are exactly $k$ insensitive distributions in the closed simplex.
All $k$ are interior and have distinct levels. These open sets can be
chosen arbitrarily close to $D=0$.
no_target_yet.title: Nonuniqueness in Vega Coso's question on accidental neutrality

no_target_yet.reason: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.statement:
There are fixed data with $N=m=2$ and a nonempty relatively open
subset $U\subset\mathcal D$ such that every $D\in U$ is admissible,
$A,B>0$, no column of $B$ is proportional to a column of $A$,
and there is an interior distribution $q\ne\pi$ insensitive
at a level different from $c_0$. Consequently no dense subset of
$\mathcal D$ can have global uniqueness for these data.
